The app is built and committed. Here's what was created:

### Architecture

**Render mode: `InteractiveAuto`** — pages SSR on first visit (fast paint), then switch to WebAssembly so all subsequent interaction runs client-side with zero server round-trips. Perfect for worldwide users.

### Project structure

```
ShipmentTracker/
├── ShipmentTracker/              # Server project
│   ├── Api/ShipmentEndpoints.cs  # REST API (role-scoped)
│   ├── Data/
│   │   ├── Shipment.cs           # Entity model
│   │   ├── ApplicationUser.cs    # Extended with Role field
│   │   ├── SeedData.cs           # 5 sample shipments
│   │   └── Migrations/           # EF Core migration
│   └── Components/
│       └── Account/CustomClaimsPrincipalFactory.cs
├── ShipmentTracker.Client/       # WebAssembly project
│   ├── Models/ShipmentDto.cs     # Shared DTO
│   └── Pages/
│       ├── Shipments.razor       # Dispatcher dashboard
│       └── Tracking.razor        # Customer tracking page
```

### Key features

| Feature | Implementation |
|---|---|
| **Dispatcher dashboard** | Filter by status, search, create shipments, update status inline |
| **Customer tracking** | Search by tracking #, visual progress timeline, card view of own shipments |
| **Auth** | ASP.NET Identity with `Role` claim (`Dispatcher`/`Customer`); API enforces role-scoped access |
| **Performance** | Auto render mode = SSR → WASM; no server round-trips after initial load |
| **Database** | SQLite + EF Core, auto-migrated and seeded on startup |

Run with `dotnet run --project ShipmentTracker`.
